Oh, I just noticed that my formulation was ambiguous: I wasn't talking about the big untangling (this surely needs to be done some time, but not in this pr), I was only talking about finding the right location inside the spaghetti, where the code from e_os.h fits best. :grin:

You don't have to find the *best* place to put the code, just a *working* place.  For example, putting it right after the include's and before anything else should be fine.  (Why is an exercise for the reader)

Thanks for your hints @richsalz. TBH, it was just an excuse to hide the fact that I was too much distracted with other things like organizing OMC meetings and reviewing other PRs, which prevented me from making progress here...

> You don't have to find the _best_ place to put the code, just a _working_ place. For example, putting it right after the include's and before anything else should be fine. (Why is an exercise for the reader)

The situation was not that simple, I couldn't just place it "after the includes". I had to place it in the middle of the includes, high enough to ensure that the shared memory headers get included: 

https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/604ee9fa4981f9166852735826249081ad26c359/crypto/rand/rand_unix.c#L74-L77

It's not ideal, but it works. _(And again the entanglement of rand_unix.c increases with every new piece which is added to it. Time to clean it up...)_
Sigh.  I did so much work to clean up the ifdef nonsense back in the day.

> Sigh. I did so much work to clean up the ifdef nonsense back in the day.

What an irony that the second law of thermodynamics also applies to rand_unix.c: The more entropy (=mess) the file contains, the more it increases with every new piece you add.
Maybe we should feed the excessive #ifdef entropy into the DRBG? 🤣

Merged, thanks!

Instead of defining the randomness sources by _operating system_, could we instead define them by _source_.  I.e. rand_device.c, rand_rdrand.c, rand_rdtsc.c, ...  The #ifdef maze could then be mostly avoided.

issue_context.title: refactor random-related stuff out of e_os.h
issue_context.body: I think only the crypto/rand files need the random stuff, so you can move 45 lines out of e_os.h to a separate file, or perhaps crypto/rand/rand_local.h ?

review_comments:
_FWIW @levitte: when checking indented #ifdef blocks with Emacs, its lax interpretation of whitespace (\<space> matches any sequence of whitespace characters) can become quite annoying. To turn it off, you can add the following lines to your .emacs file:_

```
(setq isearch-lax-whitespace nil)
(setq isearch-regexp-lax-whitespace nil)
```
